question: What haemoglobin threshold defines anaemia in a pregnant woman according to the World Health Organization?
explanation: The World Health Organization sets the lower limit of normal haemoglobin for pregnant women at 11.0 g/dL, below which a diagnosis of anaemia is made. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h1)

question: Why does low haemoglobin cause a major risk during active labour?

options.B: It causes premature rupture of the membranes
options.C: It decreases the oxygen-carrying capacity needed during contractions

explanation: Uterine contractions temporarily reduce blood flow to the placenta, so the mother needs enough oxygen reserve to prevent fetal distress. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h1)

question: Which part of maternal blood increases much more than red blood cells during pregnancy?
explanation: Plasma volume expands by nearly 50%, which is much more than the increase in red blood cells, leading to normal pregnancy dilution. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h2)

question: How does the heart compensate for fewer red blood cells during pregnancy?

options.A: By reducing total peripheral resistance drastically
options.B: By decreasing systemic blood pressure permanently
options.C: By slowing down the resting heart rate

explanation: To keep tissues supplied with enough oxygen even with fewer red blood cells, the heart pumps a larger volume of blood each minute. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h2)

question: A pregnant woman with a haemoglobin level of 8.5 g/dL has which category of anaemia?
explanation: Haemoglobin values between 7.0 and 9.9 g/dL are classified clinically as moderate anaemia. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h3)

question: At what haemoglobin level is anaemia considered a life-threatening emergency?
explanation: Severe anaemia is defined as a haemoglobin level below 7.0 g/dL, which needs urgent care to prevent heart failure. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h3)

question: What is the leading cause of anaemia among pregnant women in Nigeria?
explanation: Poor dietary intake combined with the high iron demands of pregnancy makes iron deficiency the top cause of anaemia. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h4)

question: How does chronic malaria directly cause anaemia in pregnancy?

options.A: By increasing the renal excretion of dietary iron
options.B: By causing continuous and severe pulmonary haemorrhage
options.C: By blocking the intestinal absorption of folic acid
options.D: By destroying red blood cells and suppressing the bone marrow

explanation: Malaria parasites break down red blood cells as they multiply, and the body's immune response slows down the making of new cells. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h4)

question: Which postpartum complication is a major risk for a woman who enters labour with severe anaemia?
explanation: A muscle lacking enough oxygen cannot contract strongly enough to squeeze blood vessels shut after delivery, leading to uterine atony. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h5)

question: How does maternal anaemia primarily affect the baby during labour?

options.A: It accelerates fetal skeletal maturation inside the uterus
options.B: It causes chronic intrauterine hypoxia and fetal distress
options.C: It increases the likelihood of congenital limb defects
options.D: It triggers spontaneous passage of meconium pre-term

explanation: Low maternal oxygen levels limit what gets passed through the placenta, reducing oxygen to the baby during contractions. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h5)

question: Which physical area is commonly checked for palmar pallor during a quick nursing assessment?
explanation: Palmar creases, the inside of the lower eyelids, and nail beds are checked for pallor because they have many tiny surface blood vessels. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h6)

question: Why is physical check alone not enough to diagnose anaemia in a labouring woman?

options.A: It requires the patient to be under general anaesthesia
options.B: Physical examination alters the maternal blood pressure
options.C: Pallor only appears after delivery has concluded
options.D: Clinical signs of pallor can be subjective and unreliable

explanation: Skin tone and poor surface blood flow can hide palmar pallor, so a blood test is needed for a true diagnosis. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h6)

question: What is an immediate nursing priority when an anaemic patient is admitted to the labour ward?
explanation: Setting up an IV line early ensures the team can quickly give fluids or blood if bleeding happens. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h7)

question: Why should a labouring woman with anaemia lie on her side?

options.A: To reduce the intensity of painful uterine contractions
options.B: To prevent compression of major blood vessels by the uterus
options.C: To speed up the process of complete cervical dilation
options.D: To prevent the premature rupture of amniotic membranes

explanation: Lying on the side stops the heavy uterus from pressing on major blood vessels, keeping blood flowing well to the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h7)

question: What is the primary medication used right after delivery to prevent heavy bleeding?
explanation: Oxytocin is the standard drug given to help the uterus contract firmly and lower blood loss after childbirth. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h8)

question: Which sign is an early indicator of shock in an anaemic woman with postpartum bleeding?
explanation: The heart beats faster first to make up for dropping blood volume before blood pressure starts to fall. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h8)
